\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سوار} (savār)}{سوار (savār)}]{\ur{سوار} (savār) — on board; riding}

\label{lesson:UR-C389-savar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a berth (on a train), then the Urdu for to gaze (at).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سوار}}
\textbf{\ur{سوار}} — \emph{savār} — \textquotedblleft{}on board; riding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہم} \ur{صبح} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{میں} \ur{سوار} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ham subah gāṛī meṅ savār the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We were on board the train in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
is usually traced to Persian \emph{savār}, \textquotedblleft{}a rider, mounted\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu a passenger who has got on a bus or a train is \textbf{\ur{سوار}} too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ham subah gāṛī meṅ savār the.} — We were on board the train in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a berth (on a train), then the Urdu for to gaze (at), then say \emph{savār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سوار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}On board; riding\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گٹھری} (gaṭhrī)}{گٹھری (gaṭhrī)}]{\ur{گٹھری} (gaṭhrī) — a bundle (tied in cloth)}

\label{lesson:UR-C389-gathri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to gaze (at), then the Urdu for on board.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گٹھری}}
\textbf{\ur{گٹھری}} — \emph{gaṭhrī} — \textquotedblleft{}a bundle (tied in cloth)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ایک} \ur{مسافر} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{کپڑوں} \ur{کی} \ur{گٹھری} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek musāfir ke pās kapṛoṅ kī gaṭhrī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
One passenger had a bundle of clothes.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گٹھری}} (\emph{gaṭhrī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{gaṭhṛī}, \textquotedblleft{}a bundle\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{grathna}, \textquotedblleft{}a bunch\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4348).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرکانا} (sarkānā)}{سرکانا (sarkānā)}]{\ur{سرکانا} (sarkānā) — to slide (something) along}

\label{lesson:UR-C389-sarkana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for on board, then the Urdu for a bundle (tied in cloth).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سرکانا}}
\textbf{\ur{سرکانا}} — \emph{sarkānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to slide (something) along\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنا} \ur{تھیلا} \ur{سیٹ} \ur{کے} \ur{نیچے} \ur{سرکایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne apnā thailā sīṭ ke nīche sarkāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I slid my bag under the seat.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{گٹھری} \ur{آگے} \ur{سرکائی}, \emph{us ne gaṭhrī āge sarkāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سرکانا}} (\emph{sarkānā}) is built on \emph{saraknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to slide\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{sarati}, \textquotedblleft{}runs, glides\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13250): this is the form for moving something else.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarkānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne apnā thailā sīṭ ke nīche sarkāyā.} — I slid my bag under the seat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for on board, then the Urdu for a bundle (tied in cloth), then say \emph{sarkānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جماہی} (jamāhī)}{جماہی (jamāhī)}]{\ur{جماہی} (jamāhī) — a yawn}

\label{lesson:UR-C389-jamahi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a bundle (tied in cloth), then the Urdu for to slide (something) along.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جماہی}}
\textbf{\ur{جماہی}} — \emph{jamāhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a yawn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رات} \ur{لمبی} \ur{تھی} \ur{اور} \ur{سارا} \ur{کو} \ur{جماہی} \ur{آئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt lambī thī aur sārā ko jamāhī āī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The night was very long and Sara yawned.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جماہی}} (\emph{jamāhī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jamhāī}, \textquotedblleft{}a yawn\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{jṛmbhāyita}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5266). A yawn comes to you: \textbf{\ur{سارا} \ur{کو} \ur{جماہی} \ur{آئی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a bundle (tied in cloth), then the Urdu for to slide (something) along, then say \emph{jamāhī} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اونگھنا} (ūṅghnā)}{اونگھنا (ūṅghnā)}]{\ur{اونگھنا} (ūṅghnā) — to doze}

\label{lesson:UR-C389-unghna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to slide (something) along, then the Urdu for a yawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اونگھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اونگھنا}} — \emph{ūṅghnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to doze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سارا} \ur{کھڑکی} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{بیٹھ} \ur{کر} \ur{اونگھ} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sārā khiṛkī ke pās baiṭh kar ūṅgh rahī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sara sat by the window, dozing.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{میں} \ur{اونگھا}, \emph{voh gāṛī meṅ ūṅghā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اونگھنا}} (\emph{ūṅghnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ū̃ghnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be drowsy\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{uṅghati}, \textquotedblleft{}sleeps\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 1632).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.
